correctness.rationale: Dutta–Nath Theorem 2.1 proves distinct noncentral centralizers S_i intersect precisely in the center and that Γ_R≅disjoint union K_{m_i}, m_i=|S_i|−|Z(R)|. Every dominating set meets each connected clique, so D(Γ_R,x)=∏((1+x)^{m_i}−1). With y=1+x, unique factorization Q(y)=∏(y^{m_i}−1) into cyclotomics gives E_d=∑_{d|m_i}1, and Möbius inversion recovers a_m=∑_{k≥1}μ(k)E_{km}. Thus the polynomial determines exactly every component size and graph isomorphism class among CC-ring commuting graphs. Primary Theorem 2.3 states for additive quotient R/Z(R)≅C_p² the graph is (p+1)K_{(p−1)|Z|}; recover p=t−1, center size m/(p−1), ring order p²|Z|. Independent symbolic cyclotomic reconstruction checked 194 unordered integer-partition profiles of graph orders 1..11 and independently enumerated actual UT_2(F2), UT_2(F3) commuting graphs with profiles 3K2 and 4K6. These finite checks are illustrative; all-size proof is exact UFD and Möbius inversion.

evidence: The CC-ring decomposition proves graph structure, but not uniqueness of recovering a multiset from Q(y). Complete r-partite graph D-uniqueness is about complements of cluster graphs and global uniqueness, not this inversion theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Published results do not explicitly state a dominating injectivity theorem for disjoint clique component multisets; source results alone require the cyclotomic inverse calculation.

originality.rationale: Dutta–Nath primary 2016 Theorem 2.1 establishes the CC-ring cluster graph structure and computes adjacency spectrum/genus but no domination polynomial or recovery. Jahari–Alikhani 2015/2016 studies D-equivalence, including non-cluster graphs sharing D of clique unions, so global D-uniqueness is false. The submitted theorem restricts to the naturally defined CC-ring class and proves exactly the complete inverse problem there. Relevant published Resultary entries on domination of other finite-ring graph constructions do not imply it; no inspected primary statement determines a cluster graph size multiset from domination polynomial using cyclotomic valuations.
residual_risks: Another article may explicitly prove domination-polynomial injectivity on cluster graphs under a different name; this cannot be ruled out by keyword searches.
The method uses standard Möbius inversion; value depends on specific graph reconstruction in the CC-ring class, not on novelty of factorization itself.
The theorem does not determine the underlying ring isomorphism type, nor the center order in general CC-rings.

value.rationale: The domination polynomial is not globally isomorphism-complete; proving and providing explicit reconstruction on all finite CC-ring commuting graphs gives a natural algebraically motivated positive classification. The exact center/ring order recovery on rank-two quotient adds a concrete arithmetic application. Although the proof uses standard cyclotomic factorization and Möbius inversion, the resulting complete invariant across this structurally natural class is specific, unknown from inspected prior work, and useful for comparing commuting graph invariants; it is more than an arbitrary isolated numerical computation.

limitations: Only within finite CC-ring commuting graphs; outside this family D need not imply graph isomorphism.
Even within the family the domination polynomial generally does not recover ring isomorphism.
